newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila exporters group opposes sugar tariff move.
newsitem.headline: Manila exporters group opposes sugar tariff move.

text.p: Philippine food processors and exporters opposed on Tuesday proposals by local sugar millers and planters that the government withdraw the 35 percent tariff rebate on sugar imports from neighbouring countries.

The Philippine Food Processors and Exporters Organisation Inc (Philfoodex), which has 165 members, also oppposed the recommendation by a committee headed by Executive Secretary Ruben Torres that the government increase tariff on imported sugar.

"While we can appreciate your concern for the sugar industry, its producers, traders and workers, this must not be at the expense of food processors, its supplies and its workers," Philfoodex said in a letter to Torres, a copy of which was given to reporters.

A multi-sectoral committee formed by President Fidel Ramos to address the sugar glut due to imports recently asked the Tariff Commission to raise sugar tariff to 133 percent from 100 percent from January 1 to June 30, 1997; and to 110 percent from 80 percent from July 1 to August 31, 1997.

Local sugar planters and millers also asked the government to withdraw the 35 percent tariff discount given by the Philippines on the importation of refined sugar from neighbouring Southeast Asian nations.
